html:
The Waorani, or Huaorani, are an Indigenous people of the Amazon of Ecuador, between the Napo and Curaray rivers. They number about 4,000 and speak a language isolate, related to no other known language.

For centuries they defended their forest by force against neighbours, rubber tappers and settlers, and were feared for it. In 1956 they killed five American missionaries who tried to contact them, an event widely reported in the United States. Missionaries who followed, including the widow and sister of two of the men, settled among them in the late 1950s, and most Waorani moved to a mission area. Since the 1960s oil drilling in their land has brought roads, pollution and conflict. In 2019 they won a court case that blocked oil leasing on part of their territory. Their neighbours include the Kichwa and the Shuar.
